scope: Synthetic identifiability prerequisite only. Prior body results and analytic time-change reasoning are known. No observed Martian magnetic map is fitted. No external preregistration.
question: Can a changing Poisson reversal rate be separated from unknown acquisition clocks using the declared magnetic observations?

model_families.changing_rate: Two positive Poisson rates separated at elapsed time 100 Myr; shared signed field over all bodies.
model_families.constant_rate: One Poisson rate; acquisition kernels and emplacement ages may vary in the same declared nuisance class.
model_families.nuisance_class: Positive piecewise-affine recording-time transformations with slopes 0.1 to 10. Both families allow this same class, plus source moment scales 0.5 to 2 and activity windows transformed with their acquisition clock. Main example is continuously active. Absolute geological source ages are not supplied.

counterexample.warp: u(t)=integral_0^t lambda(s)ds / lambda_constant. Split acquisition intervals at every rate break; preserve each subinterval mass. Source order and geometry unchanged.
counterexample.geometry: 24 ideal point dipoles at 20 km depth in a sphere of radius 3389.5 km; common z-directed magnetic moments of reference magnitude 1e14 A m2 times signed recorded fraction. This is a linear synthetic basis; cooling thickness is an effective temporal scale, not coupled finite dipole-body geometry.
counterexample.noise_rule: Identical additive Gaussian noise in paired equivalent realizations establishes equality of the joint observation laws; also report signal differences before noise. No noise value is calibrated to Langlais coefficient uncertainty.
counterexample.gate: Any distinct-rate pair within the declared nuisance class that agrees to relative map error <=1e-10 falsifies global identifiability in this class. No novelty or universal impossibility claim.

known_clock_positive_control.observable: Dated, instantaneous and noiseless binary polarity samples in two segments, with a declared common sample spacing; stronger information than orbital amplitudes.
known_clock_positive_control.fit: Binomial sign-change likelihood with p=(1-exp(-2*rate*dt))/2. Constant model shares p, change model fits each p independently; same boundary [0,0.5]. LRT max(0,2*(LL_change-LL_constant)). Break known, no search for a date.
known_clock_positive_control.threshold: Maximum 95th percentile LRT over the declared null rate grid, use strict > cutoff. Held-out null and alternative trials are separate.
known_clock_positive_control.success_rule: Primary n=1000 strong change 0.15 to 1.5: held-out power >=0.8 and largest held-out false positive rate <=0.075. Other lengths/contrasts are sensitivities, not selected post hoc.
known_clock_positive_control.unknown_clock_control: Likelihood depends on rate*spacing only. Repeat profiling with separate unknown segment spacings; show exact equivalent parameters, not a fabricated classifier score.

deliverables: Pathwise record and synthetic-map equality checks, with shared activity windows
Fixed-clock likelihood classification and recovery on held-out trials
A clear gate before fitting observed geology or magnetic maps
Reproducible analytic tests, figures, source notes and manifest
interpretation: A counterexample establishes non-identifiability in the stated flexible model class only. Independent acquisition ages, cooling histories and coupled material/geometry constraints can restrict that class. Passing a fixed-clock positive control does not establish those data exist for Mars. No reversal transition date or preferred Mars model is inferred.
